CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive hepatitis C lab work found on screening during routine physical.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presented after positive hepatitis C antibody test was found as part of routine physical screening. Patient reports feeling fine and was surprised by this result. Denies prior diagnosis of hepatitis C. History of intravenous drug use in the past but has been clean for over 15 years. Currently drinks beer occasionally, approximately one per day, less than in the past. Smokes one to two cigarettes per day, has cut down significantly but having difficulty quitting completely. Concerned about transmission risk to wife and children.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No other medical conditions reported. Recently completed physical examination.

MEDICATIONS
Not taking any medications.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Family history significant for hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Former intravenous drug use, clean for over 15 years. Current alcohol use, approximately one beer per day. Current smoker, one to two cigarettes per day. Married with children.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals reviewed and normal. General: no distress, no jaundice. Heart: regular rate and rhythm with grade two out of six systolic ejection murmur. Lungs: clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: bowel sounds present, soft, no splenomegaly. Musculoskeletal: no gait disturbance or edema.

RESULTS
HCV antibody: positive. Liver panel: elevated AST at 39. ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C infection confirmed by positive HCV antibody. Plan to obtain additional confirmatory testing including HCV RNA and HCV genotype. Ultrasound elastography ordered to assess for liver fibrosis and determine severity of liver disease. Will review results to determine treatment plan. Family screening recommended with HCV antibody test for wife and children, with referral to family doctor for scheduling. Follow-up appointment in three weeks.
